## Proof

Place the sphere's center at the origin, with the tower along the positive z-axis. The sphere has radius $R = 156$ ft, so the top of the sphere is at $(0,0,156)$. The tower is 13 ft tall, so the observation point (top of tower) is
$$T = (0, 0, 169).$$

Let $P$ be a point on the horizon — a point on the sphere where the line of sight from $T$ is tangent to the sphere. Tangency means $\overrightarrow{TP}$ is perpendicular to the radius $\overrightarrow{OP}$, i.e.
$$(T - P)\cdot P = 0.$$

Parametrize $P$ by colatitude $\theta$ (measured from the top of the sphere):
$$P = (R\sin\theta,\, 0,\, R\cos\theta) = (156\sin\theta,\, 0,\, 156\cos\theta).$$

Then
$$T - P = (-156\sin\theta,\, 0,\, 169 - 156\cos\theta),$$
and
$$(T-P)\cdot P = -156^2\sin^2\theta + 156\cos\theta(169 - 156\cos\theta)$$
$$= -156^2\sin^2\theta + 156\cdot 169\cos\theta - 156^2\cos^2\theta$$
$$= -156^2(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) + 156\cdot 169\cos\theta$$
$$= -156^2 + 156\cdot 169\cos\theta.$$

Setting this to zero:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{156}{169} = \frac{12}{13}.$$

This is the familiar $5\text{-}12\text{-}13$ triangle, so
$$\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}.$$

The horizon is a circle of latitude on the sphere at colatitude $\theta$. Its radius (in 3D space) is
$$r = R\sin\theta = 156\cdot\frac{5}{13} = 12\cdot 5 = 60 \text{ ft}.$$

The drone completes one full revolution along this circle, so the distance traveled is its circumference:
$$\boxed{120\pi \text{ feet}}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE

The top of the tower is at height R + h = 156 + 13 = 169 feet above the sphere's center.

The horizon line is the set of points on the sphere visible (tangent lines of sight) from the top of the tower.

Let me set up coordinates. Center of sphere at origin. Top of sphere at (0,0,156). Tower extends upward from there, so top of tower at (0,0,169).

A point P on the sphere at angle θ from the top (colatitude). The line from tower top T=(0,0,169) to P is tangent to the sphere, meaning it's perpendicular to the radius at P.

Tangent condition: (T - P) · P = 0.

P = (R sinθ, 0, R cosθ) = (156 sinθ, 0, 156 cosθ).

T - P = (-156 sinθ, 0, 169 - 156 cosθ).

(T-P)·P = -156² sin²θ + 156 cosθ (169 - 156 cosθ) = 0
= -156² sin²θ + 156·169 cosθ - 156² cos²θ
= -156²(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 156·169 cosθ
= -156² + 156·169 cosθ = 0

So 156·169 cosθ = 156², cosθ = 156/169.

The horizon is a circle at colatitude θ where cosθ = 156/169.

The radius of this circle (on the sphere) is r = R sinθ = 156 sinθ.

sinθ = sqrt(1 - (156/169)²) = sqrt((169² - 156²)/169²) = sqrt((169-156)(169+156))/169 = sqrt(13·325)/169.

13·325 = 4225 = 65². So sinθ = 65/169.

r = 156 · 65/169.

156 = 12·13, 169 = 13². So 156/169 = 12/13.

r = (12/13)·65 = 12·5 = 60.

The circumference = 2πr = 2π·60 = 120π.

So the total distance traveled is 120π feet.

Let me double check: cosθ = 156/169 = 12/13. sinθ = 5/13 (since 5-12-13 triangle). Yes sinθ = 5/13.

r = 156 · 5/13 = (156/13)·5 = 12·5 = 60. ✓

Circumference = 120π.
